svg.title: Outer conjugacy separates finite return, modular time, and phase
svg.desc: For positive asymptotic period p, the outer class of alpha to the p is the unique modular class at time T. Subtract time T divided by p, obtain beta with both periods p and phase gamma, then reconstruct the outer conjugacy model a p gamma tensor sigma T divided by p. Zero asymptotic period has one separate class.

g.text: Separate the return time from the finite-period phase
M: separable AFD type III₁ factor · R: hyperfinite II₁ factor
1 FIND THE FIRST CENTRALLY TRIVIAL POWER
δ is central and injective in Out(M). The return time T is unique. [OMC-01–02]
β = α σ_(-T/p)^φ pₒ(β) = pₐ(β) = p
βᵖ = Ad U, β(U) = γU, γᵖ = 1. [OMC-02–03]
3 CLASSIFY β AND RESTORE MODULAR TIME
α is outer conjugate to a_(p,γ) ⊗ σ_(T/p)^ψ
Every p ≥ 1, γᵖ = 1, T ∈ ℝ occurs; the triple is complete. [OMC-04–05]
Exactly one outer-conjugacy class: a₀ ⊗ id. No finite-return pair (γ,T). [OMC-06]
Brackets denote outer classes. The normal form is up to outer conjugacy. Original figure · CC0-1.0.
